title: Evaluation formula for coextension along an invertible scalar map
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a symmetric monoidal closed category with equalizers and coequalizers, in which tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Let $R,S$ be commutative monoid objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]) and $\varphi:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ an isomorphism of monoid objects. Module objects and their morphisms are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use restriction, extension and coextension of scalars as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For an $R$-module $N$ with action $\gamma_N:R\otimes N\to N$, put $T_N=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}N$; its underlying object is $N$ and its $S$-action is $\beta_N=\gamma_N\circ(\varphi^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)$. Write $\eta_S:\mathbf1\to S$ for the unit and $\lambda_A:\mathbf1\otimes A\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ for the left unitor.

Let $E_N=\operatorname{Coext}_{\varphi}N=\operatorname{Hom}_R(S,N)$, with equalizer inclusion $\iota_N:E_N\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(S,N)$ and restricted evaluation $v_N:S\otimes E_N\to N$. The component $e_N:E_N\xrightarrow{\sim}T_N$ of the adjoint-uniqueness comparison of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension-along-iso] has underlying morphism
$$e_N=v_N\circ(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_{E_N})\circ\lambda_{E_N}^{-1}.$$
The transpose $\widehat\beta_N:N\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(S,N)$ factors uniquely through $\iota_N$ as $d_N:N\to E_N$. With the $S$-action of $T_N$ on its domain, $d_N$ is $S$-linear, $\iota_N\circ d_N=\widehat\beta_N$, and
$$e_N\circ d_N=\mathrm{id}_{T_N},\qquad d_N\circ e_N=\mathrm{id}_{E_N}.$$
Both formulas define natural transformations in $N$; in particular evaluation at the unit is the specified natural isomorphism of $S$-modules, with inverse the factored transpose of $\beta_N$.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: the two comparisons through restriction along the inverse; explicit component normalization of def-sfb-modobj-coextension-along-iso

proof.text:
Put $F=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, $H=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$ and $G=\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], both restriction functors retain underlying objects and arrows. For an $R$-module $N$, the action on $FHN$ is
$$\gamma_N\circ(\varphi^{-1}\otimes1)\circ(\varphi\otimes1)=\gamma_N.$$
For an $S$-module $M$, the action on $HFM$ similarly equals $\gamma_M\circ((\varphi\circ\varphi^{-1})\otimes1)=\gamma_M$. Thus the identity underlying arrows give natural module isomorphisms $FH\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathrm{id}\cong HF$: they are module morphisms by the action equation in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and their naturality squares are the identity square of each underlying arrow. In particular the component $b_N:FHN\to N$ has underlying arrow $\mathrm{id}_N$.

source.place: Restriction action formula, applied successively to phi and its inverse

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] to $F,H$ with the two natural isomorphisms of step 1. It gives an adjunction $b:F\dashv H$ whose counit is precisely the chosen $b_N:FHN\to N$, hence is the identity on underlying objects. The lemma keeps this counit fixed when adjusting the unit, so no arbitrary choice of equivalence data enters the normalization. All its hypotheses are supplied by step 1: these are functors between the two module categories and both composites have specified natural isomorphisms with the appropriate identity functor. These two isomorphisms are exactly the quasi-inverse data of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence] (its unit and counit are the underlying identity maps, with the same action computation as step 1), so $b$ is the adjunction that [def-sfb-modobj-coextension-along-iso] obtains from that definition through the same lemma.

source.place: Coextension comparison through the inverse restriction; make the counit normalization explicit

proof.text:
The category is closed with equalizers and $\varphi$ is a monoid morphism, so [def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction] gives $a:F\dashv G$ with counit $\varepsilon_N:F E_N\to N$ equal to evaluation at the unit. The equalizer and its evaluation are those of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. Explicitly, $v_N=\mathrm{ev}_{S,N}\circ(1_S\otimes\iota_N)$; inserting the unit into its first input gives the underlying counit
$$\varepsilon_N=v_N\circ(\eta_S\otimes1_{E_N})\circ\lambda_{E_N}^{-1}.$$
This is an equality of arrows $E_N\to N$ in $\mathcal C$, with the counit's $R$-linearity supplied by the adjunction statement. Coequalizers and the tensor-colimit hypotheses of the item are stronger than needed for this application.

source.place: Evaluation-at-unit counit; the displayed equalizer evaluation in def-sfb-modobj-coextension

proof.text:
Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to the adjunctions $a:F\dashv G$ and $b:F\dashv H$. Its comparison $e_N:GN\to HN$ is the unique $S$-module morphism satisfying
$$b_N\circ F(e_N)=\varepsilon_N.$$
By step 2 the underlying $b_N$ is the identity, and by step 1 $F$ retains arrows. Therefore the underlying $e_N$ is exactly the arrow displayed in step 3, proving the requested evaluation formula for the adjoint-uniqueness comparison, rather than merely exhibiting some isomorphism. The same cited statement supplies its inverse $\delta_N:HN\to GN$ as the $a$-transpose of $b_N$, both inverse identities, and naturality of $e$ and $\delta$ in $N$. This $e$ is the comparison specified by [def-sfb-modobj-coextension-along-iso]: that definition takes the adjunctions $a$ of step 3 and $b$ of step 2 and orients its isomorphism $\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$ by the same counit equation, so the statement's $e_N$ is the family computed here.

source.place: Counit-compatible right-adjoint comparison and its inverse, applied to restriction/coextension and inverse restriction

proof.text:
It remains to identify $\delta_N$ with the specified factored transpose. In the inverse Hom bijection of [def-sfb-modobj-restrict-coextend-adjunction], take $M=HN=T_N$ and $f=b_N:F T_N\to N$. Its underlying arrow is $\mathrm{id}_N$, so the cited formula $m\mapsto(s\mapsto f(sm))$ says, intrinsically, that
$$v_N\circ(1_S\otimes\delta_N)=\beta_N:S\otimes N\to N.$$
Transposing this equality under the closed-structure bijection of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension] gives $\iota_N\circ\delta_N=\widehat\beta_N$. Thus $\delta_N$ is a factorization of $\widehat\beta_N$ through the equalizer inclusion; uniqueness in that equalizer's universal property shows that it is the $d_N$ in the statement. It is $S$-linear because the inverse Hom bijection lands in $S$-module morphisms. Substituting $d_N=\delta_N$ into step 4 gives $e_N\circ d_N=\mathrm{id}_{T_N}$ and $d_N\circ e_N=\mathrm{id}_{E_N}$ and naturality of both formulas. No use of elements detecting arrows in $\mathcal C$ is involved: the displayed equation is the uncurry of the cited internal inverse Hom-map formula.

source.place: Inverse Hom-map formula, specialized to the identity F T_N to N; equalizer factorization via the tensor-Hom adjunction
